block_state_algebra.pass_1: m_b = max_j s_j over the CN block members
block_state_algebra.pass_2: l_b = sum_j exp(s_j - m_b); u_b = sum_j exp(s_j - m_b) * V_j
block_state_algebra.merge: nm = max(m,m_b); rho = exp(m-nm); bet = exp(m_b-nm); l = rho*l + bet*l_b; acc = rho*acc + bet*u_b
block_state_algebra.why_two_passes: exp(s_j - m_b) needs the block max, which is only known after the whole block is scored
block_state_algebra.cost_recorded: the two-pass form RE-READS V, so V is read twice per element. Holding CN tiles instead is the resource-pruning alternative in resources.py, and which wins is a measurement rather than an assumption.

score_modes.literal_fp32: k = v/rms*gamma then sum_d(k*w)/sqrt(D) -- the golden's arithmetic order
score_modes.factored_gw: gw = gamma*w hoisted once per AIV and reused across every token group and block; s = (sum_d(v*gw)/rms)/sqrt(D)
score_modes.distinction: factored_gw removes the per-element division from the reduction. The two are NOT bit-identical by construction and are never claimed to be; both are verified against the same golden.
score_modes.residency: gw residency is materialised ONCE per AIV, before the token-group loop, which is the reuse the policy exists for

resource_pruning.generated_space: family x score mode x CN x R x D-chunk x V-pipeline-versions
rejection_reasons_are_real: UB overflow: 311336 bytes needed vs 262144 available (1.19x over)
VF register pressure: 65536 bytes vs 32768 available
multi-versioned copy of D elements into a next_power_of_2(D) region cannot prove src_total == dst_total (observed failure on D=5120/7168)
resource_pruning.honest_boundary: only the R=1, single-version, full-D-chunk online configuration has DEVICE evidence; every other feasible candidate is labelled UNMEASURED rather than being presented as a result

niter_gt_1_investigation.question: why did the G50 persistent loop produce wrong results for every iteration after the first?
hypotheses_tested_and_REJECTED: loop-invariant code motion hoisting the state init: an iteration-dependent init built from the iteration variable failed identically
an iteration-dependent init built from a PER-ITERATION MEMORY value also failed identically
missing cross-iteration synchronisation: an explicit T.ascend_pipe_barrier('PIPE_ALL') at the top of each iteration changed nothing
shared-buffer reuse across iterations: allocating the buffers INSIDE the loop changed nothing (alloc_shared is hoisted to function scope regardless)
nested Pipelined constructs: fully unrolling the inner N loop changed nothing
a simple index fault: the wrong values do not match the expected output of any other token
niter_gt_1_investigation.established_by_bisection: copy-only, V-load-only, and single-reducer-online-state variants are ALL correct at niter=2. The fault first appears when the SCORE path adds a SECOND reducer to the same VF region. This narrows it to the two-reducer region rather than the persistent loop's state carry.
niter_gt_1_investigation.relevance: CN is an INTRA-program block width, so G52's results never depended on this. Unchanged.
niter_gt_1_investigation.why_it_matters: G51's acceptance explicitly requires the persistent group schedule, so this must be resolved rather than worked around before G51 can claim it.
niter_gt_1_investigation.corrected_conclusion: The bisection described here narrowed the SYMPTOM to 'a second reducer in one VF region'. That was a symptom, not the cause: two reducers over the same quantity pass. The real cause is that resident gamma/w staging written before the persistent loop does not survive into later iterations. See G50's corrected PERSISTENT_LOOP_STATE_CARRY entry and G51's evidence.
niter_gt_1_investigation.keep_as_is_note: The hypotheses and their rejections are retained unchanged: they are what was actually tested, and erasing them would hide how the wrong narrowing arose.

not_claimed: The persistent g += P schedule across token groups (G51). All G52 results use one token group per program.
Performance: no cycle timings, no bandwidth, no ranking of CN=1 vs CN=4 vs CN=8. All pass; none is claimed faster.
R > 1 token rows per program: generated and judged as candidates but NOT executed on device.
Multi-versioned V pipelining (v_versions > 1) on device: generated and pruned, not measured.
D-chunking across multiple chunks on device: the measured kernel stages a full padded D per block.
resident_n with N large enough to exceed UB: pruned as infeasible, not attempted.
Bit-identity between literal_fp32 and factored_gw: they differ by construction.

twins.cn1_online_regression: MATCHED (the G50 kernel is emitted by a separate function and is unchanged)

clauses_added_for_CN: block state m_b (st[7]) and l_b (st[8]) must be present, or the merge has nothing to merge
a SEPARATE block accumulator u_b must exist; folding the block into the running acc would make the merge meaningless
the cross-block merge must update m, l and acc together
CN>1 must have two V copy sites each inside a range(CN) loop -- dropping the second pass silently means holding the block, which is resident_n's cost not blocked_online's
the emitted CN must equal the declared CN
scheduled_hir_and_twins.note: the two checker clauses that first fired on the CN twins were CHECKER defects (the CN=1 textual patterns did not match the blocked form), not kernel defects; both were fixed by accepting the two legal aggregation forms and by counting copy SITES rather than assuming one copy per N element
